summary.value: The cliffside communities of the highland roads, watched over by the Sun-Crown Griffin — road guardian, weather shepherd, and protector of the roosts. Its gusts normally guide travelers away from dangerous drops; against the hero, the same winds herd him back toward the exit he refuses to take.

sharedOpinions.reason: He fights the wind that is trying to save his footing and calls it an ambush. The roads will keep guiding him, whether or not he ever thanks them.
Her caravans use our high passes in the cool season; our fledglings winter on her warm stone. Old road-friends.
Rockslides are our emergency, and theirs. They climb better than anything that size has a right to.

examples.value: The wind is never against you; it is only going somewhere you have not chosen.
A road is a promise the mountain makes to strangers.

meaning.value: The Griffin's work of turning storms aside from the roads and roosts. Travelers schedule whole seasons around its rounds.
A feather of the Sun-Crown, given to trusted road-wardens as a token of safe conduct. The hero covets one as a 'boss unique'; it is a traveler's pass.

customs.value: Any traveler on the high roads is met at the first roost with water and a weather report. No one walks the passes unwarned.
At the Griffin's molt, found feathers are gathered and returned to the roosts — all but the road-feathers, which are given away deliberately.

taboos.value: Never push any creature toward a drop, even in jest. On the high roads, the edge is the only enemy anyone acknowledges.
Never climb to a roost uninvited. The nests are nurseries first and fortresses never.
